milestone.title: External review batch follow-ups (approved group) — M81/M91/M94/M96/M104/M106/M107 findings

intent.outcome: The actionable findings from the 2026-07-05 external code-review batch's approved-group milestones (M81, M91, M94, M96, M104, M106, M107) are addressed in code, docs, and tests. M108 and M109 had zero findings and are not in scope. The highest-priority item is M104 ER-3 (two missed lifecycle gate-read sites) because it MUST land before the deferred bulk lifecycle migration is applied to the dogfood plan, otherwise `mp milestone set-status` emits false G7/G8 errors.

problem.description: The 2026-07-05 external review batch produced 14 per-milestone reports (docs/code-review/M*-external-review.md) plus SUMMARY.md. Six of the approved-group milestones carried actionable findings beyond pure nits: M104 ER-3 (medium, latent post-migration gate-read miss), M96 ER-1 (medium, CHANGELOG 'unreleased' header for a shipped GA), M91 ER-1/ER-2 (medium, stale help copy + narrow-width active-tab clip), M106 ER-5 (low, unbounded drain buffer — the only M106 finding not already fixed downstream), M107 ER-1/ER-2 (low, ungated use import + §3 doc drift), plus low-severity items on M81 and M94. None block the milestones as shipped (they are all approved), but they should be cleared rather than left to rot. This milestone bundles them so they ship together with consistent regression coverage.

in_scope: M104 ER-3: reroute the two gate-read sites in validate_milestone_start_execution (gates.rs:194-200 builds done_ids from raw execution_status) and set_execution_status done-arm (milestone.rs:748 reads raw spec_status != verified) through the already-pub effective_spec_status / effective_execution_status helpers. This unblocks mp milestone set-status on migrated milestones and is a hard prerequisite for the deferred bulk lifecycle migration.

M106 ER-5: cap the pipe_drain_thread buffer (ac_verify.rs pipe_drain_thread ~:505-540) at a generous ceiling (e.g. 1MB) with a '<output truncated at N bytes>' sentinel; correct the doc comment that currently claims the 4KB chunk size 'keeps memory bounded' (it bounds lock hold time, not total buffer size). Display layer already truncates to 2000 chars so the tail is never shown.

M107 ER-1: gate the `use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt` import at ac_verify.rs:12 with #[cfg(unix)] to match the already-gated process_group(0) call site. Currently the unconditional import breaks Windows builds at the import itself before the gated call site is reached.

M107 ER-2: update verifier-cancellation.md §3 item 3 to match the F-2 waitpid-based regression test (currently still describes the kill(-pid,0) ESRCH probe and a 3s budget that the test does not use; test asserts waitpid WIFSIGNALED/WTERMSIG and elapsed < 1s). Add the audit-log pointer matching the §2a pattern.

M91 ER-1: refresh the in-app help overlay and footers — replace stale 'Navigate sidebar lanes' copy (render.rs:1643) and add Page Up/Down + mouse wheel rows (AC-09 obligation not met by the walkthrough-doc-only S7 commit). Tighten s4_help_overlay_documents_tab_bar_keys_not_sidebar_keys to assert !contains('sidebar lanes') and that the help body references Page Up/Down.

M91 ER-2: harden compute_tab_bar_layout narrow-width overflow (render.rs:148-218) so the active tab label is never entirely clipped at widths 7-14; lower the width<6 ultra-narrow guard to also fire when active_label_width+1 > width. Add a parametrized regression test over width in 6..=16 x active in {Overview, Milestones, Board}.

M91 ER-3: fix the list-row mouse click off-by-one in runner.rs:289-293 (saturating_sub(2) should be saturating_sub(3) to account for the block top border/title row inside the content area). Verify against Board/Overview which render without a list block.

M91 ER-4: remove the dead Event::GoToBoard dispatch arm (runner.rs:467-469) and the event.rs:38 mapping now that the global 'b' handler at runner.rs:146 short-circuits it; leave the global handler as the single source of truth.
M96 ER-1: stamp the CHANGELOG.md v2.0.0 GA section header with its ship date (currently '## v2.0.0 (unreleased) — 2.0 GA' for a shipped GA).
M96 ER-2: delete the duplicate '## v2.0.0-rc.4 (2026-07-01)' header at CHANGELOG.md:189.
M96 ER-3: add rc.5/rc.6 entries to the GA section's rc history bridge (currently documents rc.1-rc.4 only, omitting the two most recent rc cuts before GA).

M94 ER-1: make idempotent/no-op bulk ops a true no-op — with_milestone_mut_unlocked (milestone.rs:298-308) currently always sets updated=today() and rewrites the file even when nothing changed; skip the write when the mutated doc is byte-equal to the loaded doc.
M94 ER-2: avoid cloning the whole depends_on graph per add-depends-on target in bulk (depends_on_creates_cycle_in_graph, O(N²) per batch); pass the pre-built snapshot graph through the bulk path.

M94 ER-3: relax the TOCTOU docstring on the cycle check now that M113's advisory plan-write lock serializes writes; rephrase from 'graph may be stale' to the accurate 'serialized by the plan-write lock'.

M94 ER-4: when both --ids and --where are passed to mp milestone bulk, resolve --ids alone if --where has no matches (or emit a warning) rather than aborting the whole command on a bogus --where entry.

M81 ER-1: replace the 'bf add → bf done' shorthand in docs/concepts/02 - Getting Started/SIZE-ROUTING.md:9 with the full 'mp track add bugfix … → mp track done bugfix BF-NN' form used elsewhere in the same doc.

Cross-cutting tracking item: the Pattern 1 'AC passed but code absent' reconciliation for the changes-requested group (M100/M101/M102/M103) is deliberately deferred per the 2026-07-05 review decision and is tracked there — NOT in this milestone. Document this scope boundary in the milestone's own design decisions so future readers don't expect it here.
out_of_scope: The changes-requested group (M95, M100, M101, M102, M103) — those are reopened with their own findings; their remediation is separate.
M108 and M109 — zero findings in the external review.

Adding a 'critical' severity level to the mp reviews finding schema (the M100 ER-1 finding had to be filed as 'high' because the schema only accepts high/medium/low). Minor mp-tooling gap; filed as a dogfood observation, not gated here.
Re-statusing the mis-stamped ACs/findings on M100/M101/M102/M103 (the user explicitly deferred this to separate triage; the reopen + new findings is the chosen signal).

design_decisions.choice: One hygiene milestone covering all approved-group findings, rather than per-area splits (TUI / infra / docs).
design_decisions.rationale: The findings are individually small (the largest is M104 ER-3 at two one-line reroutes). Bundling keeps the review/complete overhead to one cycle and lets the regression tests share fixtures. The user explicitly chose the consolidated option from the 2026-07-05 scope question.

design_decisions.choice: Treat AC-01 (M104 ER-3) as the load-bearing item and land it first.
design_decisions.rationale: The two missed gate-read sites in validate_milestone_start_execution / set_execution_status done-arm are latent only because the dogfood plan still has legacy fields populated. They activate the moment the deferred bulk lifecycle migration (M100 follow-up) clears spec_status/execution_status. AC-01 also unblocks mp milestone reopen/set-status on migrated milestones (see mp-dogfood-log 2026-07-05 entry) — the bug that prevented a clean reopen of M95/M101/M103 in this very session.

design_decisions.choice: The mis-stamped ACs and wrongly-fixed internal findings on M100/M101/M102/M103 are NOT reconciled in this milestone.
design_decisions.rationale: Per the 2026-07-05 review decision, the changes-requested group is reopened with new external-review findings as the signal; re-statusing the existing ACs/findings is deferred to separate triage. Recording this boundary here so future readers don't expect the reconciliation in this milestone.

design_decisions.choice: 1MB ceiling on the drain buffer, sentinel-truncated.
design_decisions.rationale: Display layer already truncates to 2000 chars, so the tail is never shown; 1MB is well above realistic cargo test output (a few MB worst case for --workspace) while protecting constrained CI runners (2GB GitHub Actions) from OOM under broad-scope verifications. Sentinel preserves the 'something was emitted' signal.

findings.description: Review-substance has no first-class home in mp. The execution agent's self-review for M124 was written to an ad-hoc 'REVIEW-HANDOFF-M124.md' sidecar at the repo root and pointed to from the reviews.json 'notes' string. That file is not defined by mp, not validated, not surfaced by 'mp reviews show'/'mp reviews status', and is invisible to all read commands. Root cause: mp reviews offers only a one-line 'notes' field (too thin for a findings matrix) plus severity-scoped 'mp reviews finding' entries (no free-form thread/comments/handoff narrative). Agents are forced to invent sidecar files to carry review substance. Filed as BF-06 in the bugfix track for the structural fix (comments + handoffs as first-class review primitives on milestones). This finding records the M124 incident as evidence.
findings.author: zcode/GLM-5.2 (external review)

findings.description: with_milestone_mut_unlocked idempotency check (milestone.rs:329-335) serializes the in-memory MilestoneFile via serde_json::to_string_pretty WITHOUT calling prepare_for_disk(), then compares against original_raw read from disk (which WAS prepared on last write). The comparison is byte-equal today ONLY because WorkPackage.steps is #[serde(skip_serializing)] and all other normalization is symmetric — so the unprepared and prepared forms happen to serialize identically. I verified empirically against M124 (8 steps, 8 WPs): three consecutive no-op bulk set-priority ops left the file mtime unchanged and same=true in the comparison. So the code is correct, but the equivalence rests on an invariant that is not asserted anywhere: if any future field gains an asymmetric normalize-on-write (prepare_for_disk-style) without a matching skip_serializing, the idempotency check will silently start reporting changed=true on every no-op, defeating ER-1. Suggested hardening: either (a) call prepare_for_disk() on a clone before serializing for the comparison so the check compares prepared-vs-prepared, or (b) add a unit test that asserts to_string_pretty(prepared) == on_disk_raw for a fixture with steps.
